title: Very tame quotient and its Kummer charts
statement:
Let $(X,M)$ be a Noetherian fs log regular scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] with an admissible, generically free action of a finite group $G$. Admissible means that $X$ is covered by $G$-invariant affine opens; generically free means free on a dense invariant open. Assume the action is very tame: each geometric inertia group has order invertible in the residue field and acts trivially both on the characteristic monoid and on the strict local log stratum $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O^{\rm sh}_{X,\bar x}/I_{\bar x})$, with $I_{\bar x}$ generated by nonunit log sections. Then the scheme quotient $q:X\to Y=X/G$ exists, is finite surjective with orbit geometric fibres and invariant structure sheaf, and
$$M_Y=(q_*M)^G$$
is an fs log regular structure. The log morphism $q$ is Kummer etale: it is log etale in [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale], and its characteristic monoid maps are injective with every target element having a positive multiple in the image. Etale locally on strict localizations at $\bar x$ and its image this map is the strict base change of $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[B]\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[A]$, for an injective map of fs monoids $A\to B$ with every element of $B$ having a positive multiple in $A$ and with finite group cokernel annihilated by an integer invertible on the base. If $X\to S$ is an invariant log morphism, it factors uniquely through $Y\to S$.

source.place: VI 2.1--2.3 and Theorem 3.2, Proposition 3.5 and its proof, pp.71--75. The invariant log structure and standard Kummer chart are explicitly given there.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-tame-admissible-scheme-quotient] to the underlying $G$-scheme: admissibility supplies its invariant affine cover, and very tameness supplies its prime-to-residue-characteristic inertia hypothesis. It gives a Noetherian scheme quotient $q:X\to Y$, finite surjective with geometric orbit fibres and $\mathcal O_Y=(q_*\mathcal O_X)^G$, and its categorical property. Put $N=(q_*M)^G$. This is a log structure: an invariant section whose structural image is a unit is an invariant unit, and the inverse of an invariant unit is invariant; the identification of structural units is therefore $N\cap\mathcal O_Y^\times=\mathcal O_Y^\times$.

source.place: VI Theorem 3.2 and paragraph after Proposition 3.5, printed pp.74–75

proof.text: Fix $\bar x$ and $\bar y=q(\bar x)$, and put $H=\operatorname{Stab}_G(\bar x)$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$. Apply [lem-per-finite-quotient-strict-local-invariants]: $B=A^H$, $A$ is finite over $B$, and $N_{\bar y}=M_{\bar x}^H$. These are strict local rings at geometric points, not invariants under the stabilizer of an ordinary point. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian], $A$ and $B$ are Noetherian. Write $Q=\overline M_{\bar x}$ and $I$ for the nonunit log ideal. Log regularity gives $A/I$ regular and $\dim A=\dim(A/I)+\operatorname{rank}Q^{\rm gp}$.

source.place: VI paragraph after 3.5 and proof 3.7(b), printed pp.74–75

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-very-tame-equivariant-sharp-chart] to obtain the $H$-equivariant sharp fs chart $a:Q\to M$ and diagonal pairing $\chi$ with fixed roots of unity. Its hypotheses are exactly invertibility of $n=|H|$ and triviality on $Q$. The further very-tame hypothesis is triviality on $A/I$, where $I=(a(u):u\ne0)A$. Apply [lem-per-very-tame-local-kummer-quotient] using the finite extension of Step 2. It gives $P=Q\cap L$ with $P$ sharp fs, $P^{\rm gp}=L\supset nQ^{\rm gp}$, finite index, a pointed etale-local chart of the actual $N$, and $B/J\simeq A/I$, where $J=(a(p):p\ne0)B$. In particular $N$ is fs, since the neighbourhood clause supplies a chart at every $\bar y$. Also $nu\in P$ for every $u\in Q$, directly from $\chi_{nu}=\chi_u^n=1$.

The finite injective extension $B\hookrightarrow A$ is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]; [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-dimension-equal] gives $\dim B=\dim A$. The finite-index inclusion $P^{\rm gp}=L\subset Q^{\rm gp}$ gives equal rational ranks, because $nQ^{\rm gp}\subset L$. Hence
$$\dim B=\dim(A/I)+\operatorname{rank}Q^{\rm gp}=\dim(B/J)+\operatorname{rank}P^{\rm gp}.$$
The quotient $B/J$ is regular by the stratum isomorphism. As $P$ identifies with the characteristic of $N$ at $\bar y$, $J$ is precisely its nonunit log ideal. Thus the stratum and dimension conditions of [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] hold at every geometric point, proving that $(Y,N)$ is log regular. This argument does not require $X$ to be integral or to come with a preselected global pair.

Set $C=B\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q]$. By [lem-per-tame-diagonal-standard-closed-immersion], whose quotient, chart, fixed-root, and trivial-stratum hypotheses were checked in Steps 1–3, the comparison $C\to A$ is surjective and is represented etale locally by a strict closed immersion. If $q_1,\ldots,q_s$ generate $Q$, then $nq_i\in P$. Reducing each coefficient of a monomial expression modulo $n$ shows that the finitely many $z^{\sum r_iq_i}$, $0\le r_i<n$, generate $C$ as a $B$-module. Thus $C$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian], and $B\to C$ is injective since its composite with $C\to A$ is the inclusion $B\hookrightarrow A$.

The ring $C$ is strictly henselian local. Indeed, apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product] to its finite algebra over strictly henselian $B$. In the closed fibre, every nonzero monomial is nilpotent, since $(z^u)^n=z^{nu}$ with $0\ne nu\in P$ maps to zero in the residue field. Here $nu\ne0$: saturation and sharpness imply that $Q^{\rm gp}$ is torsion free, since $nv=0$ puts both $v,-v$ in $Q$, so $v$ is a unit. There are finitely many monoid generators, so the ideal of nonzero monomials in this fibre is nilpotent and the quotient is $k=B/\mathfrak m_B$. The finite henselian product therefore has exactly one factor with residue field $k$; hence $C$ is henselian local with separably closed residue field. The standard chart $P\to Q$ on $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is injective, is Kummer, has group cokernel killed by $n$, and has identity comparison morphism. The strict localization $\operatorname{Spec}B\to Y$ is ind-etale locally on source and target, so by [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance] its strict localization at every geometric point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is the strict localization of $Y$ at the image geometric point, and the pulled-back log structure, which has the chart $P$ by Step 3, has the same stalks there; hence the stratum and dimension conditions proved for $(Y,N)$ in Step 4 hold at every geometric point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Apply [lem-per-invertible-kummer-chart-log-regular] to this log regular $(\operatorname{Spec}B,P)$: $\operatorname{Spec}C$ with chart $Q$ is log regular.

The strictly local log regular ring $C$ is a domain. To see this without assuming regularity of its underlying scheme, apply [lem-trf-log-regular-completed-chart] to its closed geometric point. Its completion is one of the sharp fs formal-monoid models specified there. Both models are domains by [lem-trf-log-regular-saturation-normality], including the mixed-characteristic quotient. The completion map $C\to\widehat C$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat] and injective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] with module $C$. Thus $C$ embeds in a domain and is itself a domain. The choice of chart in the completed-model theorem is irrelevant to this conclusion.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] to $B\hookrightarrow C$ and [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-dimension-equal] to get $\dim C=\dim B=\dim A$. These dimensions are finite because the rings are Noetherian local; this finiteness is also included in [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension]. The surjection $C\to A$ of Step 5 is injective: if its kernel were nonzero, every prime containing it would be nonzero in the domain $C$. A maximal-length chain of primes in $A$ would lift to a chain in $C$ which could be extended at the bottom by $(0)$, contradicting $\dim C=\dim A$. Hence $C\simeq A$. Together with strictness, this proves the required strict-local cartesian monoid chart, rather than merely a closed immersion into a standard cover.

source.place: VI proof 3.7(c), last sentence, printed p.76

proof.text: Use the pointed etale neighbourhood comparison which is a strict closed immersion in Step 5. By the strict-localization clause of [lem-per-tame-diagonal-standard-closed-immersion], its map on strict local rings at the selected geometric points is the map $C\to A$, which is the isomorphism proved in Step 8; for a closed immersion this is the base-changed quotient map, by [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian]. The ordinary local ring of the target maps faithfully flatly to its strict henselization by [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-universally-injective] with the ordinary local ring itself as module: its map into its strict henselization is injective. The closed-immersion formula says every element of its kernel ideal maps to zero in this strict henselization, since the base-changed quotient map is an isomorphism. Injectivity therefore makes the ordinary localized kernel zero. The target is Noetherian, so finitely many generators of the kernel are each killed by a denominator outside the selected prime; restrict to their product's principal open. On that open the comparison is an isomorphism. Consequently the neighbourhood charts have etale comparison. Their injective monoid map has finite group cokernel killed by the locally invertible $n$, and $nu\in P$ for all $u\in Q$. If $Q^{\rm gp}$ has $r$ generators, this cokernel is a quotient of $(\mathbf Z/n)^r$, so its order divides $n^r$ and is invertible as required by the chart definition. The definition [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale] now gives log etaleness, while the characteristic maps are Kummer. This proves all local-chart clauses and Kummer etaleness of $q$.

Let $f:(X,M)\to(S,M_S)$ be an invariant log morphism. The categorical property of the quotient from Step 1 gives a unique underlying map $g:Y\to S$ with $f=gq$. The map of log sheaves $M_S\to f_*M=g_*q_*M$ takes values in $g_*(q_*M)^G=g_*N$ because $f$ is invariant, so it defines a log morphism $g$ compatible with the already descended structural map. Any competing log morphism has the same underlying $g$, and its log map has the same composite into $g_*q_*M$; the inclusion $N\hookrightarrow q_*M$ is injective, so the two log maps agree. This proves existence and uniqueness of the factorization.

lean.statement: theorem exists_veryTame_logQuotient (X : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X.scheme] (G : Type v) [Group G] [Finite G] (a : FSLogGroupAction G X) (hadmissible : ∀ x : X.scheme, ∃ U : X.scheme.Opens, x ∈ U ∧ IsAffineOpen U ∧ ∀ (g : G) (z : X.scheme), (a.baseAction g).hom z ∈ U ↔ z ∈ U) (hfree : a.IsGenericallyFree) (hregular : X.IsLogRegular) (hverytame : a.IsVeryTame) : ∃ (Y : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (q : EtaleLogHom X Y), IsNoetherian Y.scheme ∧ IsFinite q.base ∧ Surjective q.base ∧ a.IsQuotient q ∧ (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (x z : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X.scheme), x ≫ q.base = z ≫ q.base ↔ ∃ g : G, x ≫ (a.baseAction g).hom = z) ∧ Y.IsLogRegular ∧ q.IsLogEtale ∧ q.IsKummer ∧ (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (t : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ X.scheme), q.HasStrictLocalKummerChart t) ∧ ∀ (S : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (f : EtaleLogHom X S), (∀ g : G, (a.logMap g).CompEq f f) → ∃! r : EtaleLogHom Y S, q.CompEq r f
